pr.title: Plan project-owned device chains and the device-panel picker
pr.body:
PRIMARY USER PURPOSE — independent instrument ownership and creative continuity
The user clarified WHY this system exists: ordinary bounce/delete workflows can discard a carefully made instrument unless the user manually saves a preset first. Hex must remove that extra artistic interruption. Instrument chains are managed OUTSIDE tracks as persistent project-owned entities, not disposable track payloads or a preset-save reminder.
Required end-to-end workflow: create instrument chain -> link a track -> compose -> bounce -> delete that track -> instrument chain remains in the manager -> create a new track -> select the SAME retained chain -> continue. User must explicitly DELETE AN INSTRUMENT to remove it.
Zero linked tracks is NOT a deletion condition. Keep unassigned instrument chains in canonical project save/reopen, complete authored device/state/modulation/resource references and name/identity intact, without requiring an external preset export or relying on Undo/history recovery. Removing/bouncing/duplicating tracks must never implicitly delete or overwrite the project instrument. Missing assigned tracks do not orphan an instrument out of the saved document.
Runtime resources may suspend safely when unused under device lifecycle contracts, but this must not discard authored chain state or silently reset it on reuse. Destructive instrument deletion is an explicit separate operation with defined referenced-track handling and Undo. This independent lifetime is central acceptance, not merely an optimization or preset catalog.
Track-local devices remain track-owned; project instrument survival does not implicitly promote local effects into its state. Define any independent-copy/preset operations separately; copies alone are not a substitute for retained project-owned instruments.

CURRENT ACCEPTED DESIGN —17 October2026
The user approved this proposal after exploring audio versus MIDI routing:
- Device panel begins with a SOURCE tile/picker selecting a reusable SHARED INSTRUMENT CHAIN; track-local effects follow visually and in signal flow.
- MIDI clips drive the selected shared instrument chain. Its audio output returns to the track before LOCAL effects.
- Audio clips enter directly before those local effects; no implicit routing through the shared instrument or arbitrary internal effect suffix.
- Common reverb/shared audio effects use explicit SEND/RETURN routing. Reuse typed audio-effect/Return contracts; do not confuse shared instrument assignment with an audio-effect send.
- Selecting a track reveals its assigned source/shared chain and relevant local devices; left-side picker remains UI location. Scope must clearly distinguish shared device edits from track-local edits.
- Bounce isolates chosen track's MIDI/audio sources, excluding all others BEFORE shared processing. Include applicable shared-instrument output plus all LOCAL devices, capture POST-LOCAL / PRE-FADER. Same-track keeps fader; new-track copies original scalar fader value. Print playback avoids duplicate DSP and live-shared receive leakage; other tracks/live runtime unchanged.
- Shared send/Return contribution in bounce, automated fader curve/pan/send/output copying, bounce-to-new-track original activation and range/tail policies remain specific open details. General live shared-receiver fanout/concurrent shared-bus implications need a clear contract; source isolation during bounce is already settled.
- Hex alpha policy permits breaking format/model changes without legacy migration/backward support. Keep current-format integrity, Undo/runtime safety and user-file preservation.
This approval settles the architecture/UX direction of this PLANNING task; no broad source implementation or expansion of current native/EQ/tuning PRs has been dispatched. Focused implementation stages remain to be planned with outstanding details explicit.

User architecture/planning request,17 October2026. PLANNING ONLY; runtime implementation has not been requested through this ticket.

Outcome: decouple REUSABLE SHARED project device chains from clip-bearing tracks while ALSO retaining independent track-specific in-place device chains. User refinement: a track may receive input from a reusable shared chain and apply its own devices in a chain locked to that track. Do not migrate all devices into the shared pool or eliminate track-local processing. The plan must define both editing scopes, signal-flow stages and lifetimes. Existing audio/MIDI/hybrid tracks retain their clips. A project-owned list of instruments/device chains can be created and assigned/referenced by tracks. MIDI notes from a linked track are sent to its assigned chain. Audio out of the chain can be recorded back onto a track; user composes MIDI, bounces in place when satisfied, creates another track and links the same chain to continue reusing the setup. Preserve the original MIDI and an undoable/non-destructive workflow according to a defined bounce contract.

Latest UI direction (supersedes the initially suggested separate manager in Session/Mix): add a small extra menu/picker on the LEFT of the existing device panel for selecting project-owned device chains. Whenever a track is selected, show that track's assigned device chain in the device panel. Preserve the distinction between viewing/selecting a chain and assigning/reassigning a track; confirm ambiguous picker semantics rather than accidentally mutating assignments. Explicit empty/missing assignment and multi-selection behavior need a design. User earlier requested Tab accessibility; reconcile with current keyboard navigation/text focus and do not invent a separate full manager view or final shortcut policy.

User explicitly requested a thorough GPT-6 Astra architecture assessment for an efficient, robust system. Assessment must inspect current repository contracts and produce source-backed ownership/routing/persistence/lifecycle design, alternatives, risks, staged focused implementation plan and finite acceptance criteria before implementation. Existing per-track chain architecture must be understood before defining a clean current model.

Shared-chain refinement: the user explicitly calls the reusable chain shared, distinct from a track-locked chain. Plan the shared project-chain plus independent track-local-chain model; do not substitute presets alone. Exact concurrent runtime/event/automation semantics still need an explicit source-backed contract and any remaining user choice. Explain whether proposed runtime instances satisfy actual sharing rather than silently choosing independent copies. Distinguish sequential reuse after bounce from concurrent linked playback. Assess shared live processing vs definition/instance models and identify user-visible consequences. Also resolve MIDI owner IDs/MPE/note cleanup, conflicting automation, audio summing/output routing, per-track record/bounce isolation with nonlinear shared state/tails, feedback/cycle prevention, latency/PDC, mute/solo/arming, track-vs-chain gains and track deletion vs chain lifetime. Do not claim separate per-track stems can be recovered from one mixed nonlinear live output.

Finite planning deliverables:
1. Source-backed current/gap map and recommendation with explicit unresolved product choices, bounded real-time ownership/storage/event fanout, no callback allocation/locks/final destruction and safe topology updates.
2. Canonical project-owned chain IDs, track reference model, generic device envelopes, unknown-device preservation, a coherent current project format with atomic validation and round-trip integrity; Undo/Redo/save/reopen/copy/duplicate/delete behavior and missing references.
3. Arrangement/Session/live/record/export/bounce signal-flow contracts, note/automation isolation, shared-state and lifetime policy, latency/tails and refusal/recovery.
4. Left-side device-panel chain picker UI proposal, track selection revealing its assigned chain, creation/name/selection/assignment/edit/removal, Tab accessibility, clear shared-vs-instance feedback and existing clip/focus behavior.
5. Dependency-aware focused implementation issue/PR breakdown after decisions, targeted tests and actual optimized native acceptance; do not expand current cloud PRs.
Acceptance scenarios include creating reusable chain; authoring MIDI and rendering; recording/bounce in place; linking a new track to reuse; simultaneous links under chosen semantics; undo/save/reopen; delete/missing references; note-off/Stop/removal/tails; latency and export agreement; bounded CPU/memory; keyboard/text-focus/accessibility.

Existing related work, not duplicates: #16 native device model/runtime; #2138 freely positioned track instrument; #28 routing/automation/compensation; #26 recording/MIDI I/O; #2346 canonical track/Return capture stems; W09#2680 generic ports; W11#2682 nested racks/Instrument Grid; W05#2674 parameter/modulation semantics; W08#2677 MIDI event ownership. Project-level chain ownership is a distinct user request; racks inside a chain are a separate capability. Preserve their history, acceptance and canonical PRs. Duplicate audit read all340 returned Hex tickets and current goals; no matching project-owned chain/track-link plan found.

Mac policy: cloud implementation/checks continue independently; Mac-specific tasks are reported to coordinator and run strictly ONE local thread at a time across Hex/Yield. Sole current local slot is signing verification; this planning ticket must not start Mac builds/tests/computer use. No hosted CI, purchases or new infrastructure.
Release version intentionally unassigned pending roadmap choice. Record source links and assessment here; planning does not authorize execution.\n\n17 October2026 latest refinement — shared and track-local stages:\n- A reusable shared project device chain can provide audio input to a track. The track may ALSO own in-place devices locked to that track. Preserve the latter as a separate local processing chain.\n- Define MIDI-to-shared-chain input and shared-output-to-track-local-chain routing; assess optional audio-source/local processing paths without inventing unrequested routing defaults. Clarify shared bus output versus individual track outputs, duplicate summing, track gain/mute/solo/arming, effects/tails, shared parameter edits and independent local automation.\n- Selecting a track reveals its assigned shared chain and relevant local devices with an unmistakable shared/local edit scope. Left-side picker remains the latest UI location.\n- Record/bounce uses the track's full PRE-FADER output, including applicable shared input and track-local processing. Same-track bounce preserves the track fader; a new destination track copies the original fader value. Define selected-source isolation and preserved editable source/device state; shared nonlinear state cannot be assumed independently separable.\n- Independent create/delete/duplicate/Undo/save/reopen and missing-link handling preserve shared identity and local ownership. Track deletion must not accidentally destroy a shared chain used elsewhere.\n\n\nSUPERSEDING USER POLICY — alpha breaking changes (17 October2026): Hex remains active alpha software. Do not require backward project/model/schema compatibility or migrations until the user selects a release-worthy feature set. Breaking architecture/format changes are allowed. Remove legacy migration readers, cross-version conversion plans and historical-alpha compatibility from this plan's required work. Keep track-local chains because the requested product includes them, not to preserve an old format. Current-format validation/round-trip, explicit unsupported-format errors, Undo/runtime safety and protecting actual user files remain. Do not automatically overwrite/delete old files or expand this planning request into removing all existing migration code. Cloud4 owns a separate focused AGENTS.md policy change. Asset, tuning and shared-chain features need one coherent CURRENT format; compatibility between unpublished old branch schemas is not required.\n\n\nFIRM USER BOUNCE CONTRACT —17 October2026:\n- Bounce captures whatever the source TRACK outputs, PRE-FADER for BOTH same-track and new-track destinations. Print the applicable complete track processing path, not just instrument output.\n- Same-track bounce leaves the original track fader value unchanged.\n- Bounce to a new track sets its fader to the SAME VALUE as the original track, so the gain is not lost or applied twice and the sound retains its level.\n- Printed audio must not run through already-printed shared/local processors again, nor keep receiving a later reused shared-chain output or duplicate original MIDI playback. Define an explicit reversible source/route/device activation policy.\n- Validate audible level/output parity with asymmetric nonlinear shared/local fixtures and non-unity fader values for both destination modes; Undo/Redo/save/reopen preserve intended source and destination behavior.\n- User selected scalar fader-value copying; exact automation-curve, pan, mute/solo, send/return, bounce range and tail behavior still require a source-backed contract. Do not silently invent these as user decisions.\n\n\n
ASTRA READ-ONLY ARCHITECTURE ASSESSMENT —17 October2026
Provenance: inspected immutable main070cacc3e6bae3c16fb15e6f30a8a9d11d3c6ccd and live related issue contracts; unmerged cloud work was not treated as present. No builds/source edits by assessment.

Recommended model: project-owned SHARED chain plus track-owned LOCAL chain, with explicit typed MIDI-send and audio-receive connections. Process each shared runtime ONCE, then fan out its read-only output to independently processed local chains. Sharing means same devices, voices, effects and history; an explicit independent-copy operation could provide isolated parts. Copies are a recommendation, not an approved added feature.

Current/gap evidence:
- Track owns clips/effects/instrument/mixer/sends; project currently owns tracks/Returns/routes. Add independent chain owner instead of hidden tracks.
https://github.com/PORTALSURFER/hex/blob/070cacc3e6bae3c16fb15e6f30a8a9d11d3c6ccd/crates/hex-project/src/lib.rs#L327
- Current graph owners Track/Return and local prefix/generator/merge/suffix/fader order need shared-stage ownership.
https://github.com/PORTALSURFER/hex/blob/070cacc3e6bae3c16fb15e6f30a8a9d11d3c6ccd/crates/hex-engine/src/signal_graph.rs#L97
- Existing MIDI source fanout expands independent destination templates, NOT many sources into one shared runtime. Source note identity helps, but Expression events lack source/channel/occurrence targeting; W08 is a real required contract for isolated controller/MPE ownership.
https://github.com/PORTALSURFER/hex/blob/070cacc3e6bae3c16fb15e6f30a8a9d11d3c6ccd/crates/hex-lattice/src/instrument_runtime.rs#L38
- Current Track/Return capture has generation-bound transactional plans and Arrangement-only interactive cut; general shared/Session/live recording needs an extension.
https://github.com/PORTALSURFER/hex/blob/070cacc3e6bae3c16fb15e6f30a8a9d11d3c6ccd/crates/hex-engine/src/session_playback/capture.rs#L13
- Current MIDI conversion renders instrument only/cuts clip-duration tails and restores MIDI through Undo; it is not requested full-track bounce.
https://github.com/PORTALSURFER/hex/blob/070cacc3e6bae3c16fb15e6f30a8a9d11d3c6ccd/crates/hex-session/src/clip_conversion.rs#L15
- Device panel owns Track/Return gestures; add explicit SharedChain/TrackLocal scope with existing finalize/cancel barriers. Tab already traverses controls; include picker/scope in focus traversal rather than stealing Tab globally.
https://github.com/PORTALSURFER/hex/blob/070cacc3e6bae3c16fb15e6f30a8a9d11d3c6ccd/crates/hex-ui/src/editor/device_panel.rs#L493

Important user-visible consequence/open decision:
A shared live chain yields ONE combined output. Two receiving tracks process the SAME combined signal through different local devices/faders; they do not isolate their own MIDI contributions. Decide whether normal assignment creates one chosen audible return or deliberate multiple receivers. Never promise isolated stems from a mixed nonlinear/stateful live chain. An isolated fresh offline render is a different operation and must be labelled truthfully.

Architecture constraints:
- Distinguish MIDI source scheduling from audio processing: track-MIDI -> shared chain -> track-local audio is acyclic. Reject real typed audio/event feedback, including Returns, rather than rejecting the legitimate whole-track apparent cycle. Recording is a sink, not immediate feedback.
- No implicit second Main path for the shared chain if receiving tracks already carry its output; prevent duplicate summing.
- Persist canonical chain/device IDs, links and local state separately from viewed UI chain. Track deletion removes its links/local devices and source notes, not a shared chain used elsewhere. Referenced chain deletion must transactionally unlink or refuse clearly.
- Preserve source/channel/occurrence/generation and reserve independent terminal-note cleanup. Disconnect one source without resetting other contributors. Explicit local-vs-shared MIDI destination avoids accidentally playing both instruments. Shared parameter automation has one canonical owner/resolution rule, not callback-order competition.
- Define receiver gain/track gain/mute/solo/arming independently from contribution enablement. A soloed receiver must retain needed upstream processing; 'solo only my notes' changes shared performance and is distinct.
- Build topology/indexes/event adjacency/capture/PDC on control. Bound total shared-source voices/events/devices/connections, candidate/active/retired memory, delay/capture buffers and fanout work. No callback allocation/locks/I/O/final destruction. Late failures preserve committed DSP/clocks/ledgers/delay histories transactionally.
- Extend PDC/content-origin timing through shared fanout, local reconvergence and recording; never subtract delay twice. Retain downstream identity for old tails; routing every retired tail directly to Main can bypass local effects or double output.
- Suspend unused runtime only when supported by free-running device/modulator laws. Current serial/stereo boundary may stage implementation, but not silently exclude the requested complete workflow or required supported tracks.
- ALPHA policy: use one coherent current format, no legacy migration/backward readers required. Current-format round trip, unknown-device envelope retention, atomic failed open/edit, Undo and protecting actual files remain.

Corrected FIRM bounce implementation contract (supersedes any pre-local tap proposal):
Capture complete track output AFTER local devices and BEFORE fader, for both destination modes. Same-track retains fader; new track copies scalar source fader value. Printed audio must play AFTER already-printed processing and BEFORE that retained/copied fader via an explicit printed-playback branch or equivalent scope/range-aware bypass. Ordinary clip input would double-process local effects.
Retain source MIDI/audio/device/routing state as a restorable saved configuration (recommended non-destructive architecture). In-place printed region suppresses original contributions AND live shared receive; later reuse cannot leak onto old printed audio. Do not disable shared runtime/other tracks. Partial ranges must switch only the printed region and define history/note/tail boundaries; whole-track device bypass would break remaining live regions. One atomic Undo/Redo and save/reopen restoration.
Remaining bounce choices: original activation after new-track bounce; automated source-fader curve versus specified scalar copy; pan/balance/mute/solo/sends/output-route handling; range/preroll/tail extent. Do not claim scalar-copy tests prove full mix parity under undefined routing/automation.

Picker proposal (recommendations unless already explicit user decisions):
Left-side picker is view selection; explicit assignment action changes routing. Selecting a track shows its assigned shared chain and clearly marked local scope. Show shared usage/edit scope. Unassigned track shows no shared chain plus local devices; no track selected permits browse but disables assignment. Primary-track display for multiselection/no implicit bulk assignment. Enter/Escape and Tab/Shift-Tab preserve text/numeric focus and gesture finalization. Never replace missing identity by same-named chain.

Dependency-aware planning phases, to split into focused canonical issues after open behavior choices:
1. Resolve shared receiver/concurrency, MIDI destination, automation owner and bounce source/range policies.
2. Canonical shared/local owners, IDs/typed links, validated commands/Undo/copy/delete and CURRENT-format persistence.
3. Many-source shared runtime/event ownership and W08 expression/W05 parameter integration.
4. Shared/local graph execution/fanout, cycles, gain/solo/PDC/tails and transactional admission; integrate W09 ports. W11 nested racks are not prerequisite for initial ownership.
5. Picker, assignment/scope, selection and keyboard production UI.
6. Capture/record/print, durable media, restorable source/printed state, full/partial range transitions and Arrangement/Session/live/export agreement.
7. Integrated oracles/full exact-candidate checks and optimized native input/listening/performance via the ONE scheduled Mac lane.
Do not expand native-library/tuning cloud PRs; coordinate contracts.

Finite acceptance: concurrent same-pitch contributors/independent note-offs; receivers demonstrate common output plus different local processing; nonlinear counterexample; complete post-local/pre-fader print with unchanged/copied fader, no repeated processing or receive/MIDI leakage after reuse; Undo/save/reopen/restoration; partial printed/live transitions; held-note/tail delete/relink; Session source switches; PDC impulses/timestamps; deterministic block partitions; overflow/late-failure rollback/zero callback allocation; current-format/missing/opaque identity; picker focus/scope; measured optimized CPU/memory at representative source/receiver counts.
\n\nFIRM USER BOUNCE SCOPE —17 October2026:\nOnly the track on which the user invokes bounce is bounced. Do not automatically bounce other tracks that reference the same shared chain, replace their clips, disable their sources/receivers, change their local devices, or redirect their routing. Render the chosen track's defined complete pre-fader output and modify only its selected bounce scope/destination; shared runtime and other users remain intact. This answers which track is acted on, not the separate general live audio-receiver/fanout policy. If the chosen track receives a mixed shared-chain signal, do not silently claim its contributors have been separated. Resolve live input/contributor audition semantics explicitly before implementation, without broadening the bounce edit to other tracks.\n\n\nFIRM USER INPUT-ISOLATION CONTRACT —17 October2026 (supersedes any assumption of printing all shared contributors):\nWhen bouncing ONE chosen track, ONLY that track's MIDI/audio contribution is active in the render. Other tracks sending MIDI/audio into the same shared chain(s) are muted/excluded from that render. If the chosen track feeds multiple shared chains, render its applicable complete assigned signal path(s), including its track-local devices, without introducing other tracks' content. Do not merely solo the final receiver while upstream MIDI from other tracks keeps driving shared voices/effects.\nImplement truthful solo-source rendering with isolated/transactional render runtime and defined preroll/history: other tracks' note, controller, automation or retained-tail contributions must not contaminate the bounce. Necessary target processing remains available; define ownership of canonical chain automation separately. Do not mutate the live shared runtime/other tracks or persist their mute state as a side effect. If production uses a temporary mute mechanism, cancellation/error/success must restore exact live state.\nThis is an ISOLATED re-render of the chosen track, not extraction of its mathematically separable stem from an already mixed nonlinear live shared performance. User explicitly selected this solo-source behavior. Pre-fader/post-local tap and same-track/new-track fader rules remain firm. Only the target bounce scope/destination is changed; other tracks retain clips/devices/routes.\nAcceptance: two tracks send distinguishable notes/audio into one shared stateful/nonlinear chain; bouncing either includes only chosen source through the full intended chain/local path. Cover simultaneous same-pitch notes, shared sustain/controllers, previous other-track tails/preroll, multiple shared destinations, failure/cancel and exact project/live-state restoration; prove all excluded-source contamination absent without promising sum-of-stems equality.\n\n\nASTRA AMENDMENT — solo-source print contract:\nUse a separate offline runtime from one captured project revision. Exclude all other-track MIDI/audio/controller input BEFORE shared processing; final-output mute alone is insufficient. Initialize without other-source voices/sustain/controllers/feedback/tails; nonzero-start preroll replays ONLY the chosen contributor, not a checkpoint of mixed performance. Bound preroll and refuse unsupported history reconstruction. Retain chain-owned authored settings/automation on canonical time while excluding other-track-owned control contributions under an explicit ownership rule. Include all chosen-track shared paths exactly once, then local processing, and capture post-local/pre-fader. Never mutate live mute/solo/shared DSP. Publish durable media and prepare replacement BEFORE atomic print commit; cancellation/failure/stale source leaves live/project state unchanged. Test other-source previous held notes/sustain/long tails/audio/controllers, multiple shared paths, irregular blocks and nonzero-start automation/preroll against a clean solo-source oracle. This does not settle general concurrent live receiver fanout.\n\n\nSUPERSEDED AUDIO-BOUNCE THOUGHT —17 October2026 (user subsequently withdrew this as thinking aloud; not a fixed product requirement):\nAudio clips remain local to their track. Bouncing an AUDIO source renders that chosen track's audio through ONLY its TRACK-LOCAL device chain, then captures PRE-FADER; do not route the audio clip through the shared reusable instrument/device chain merely because the track has a shared assignment. MIDI bounce uses chosen-track MIDI into the assigned shared chain(s), followed by applicable track-local processing, with all other tracks' contributions excluded.\nSame-track fader retention and new-track scalar-fader copying apply equally. Both paths avoid double-processing already-printed devices and preserve other tracks/live state. Define hybrid-range behavior explicitly if audio and MIDI coexist: preserve these distinct source paths rather than reprocessing local audio through the shared chain. Tests must include audio-only track with a shared assignment proving shared DSP is not applied, local nonlinear effects applied exactly once, and post-local/pre-fader level parity in both destination modes.\n\n\nEARLIER EXPLORATION / RECOMMENDATION — now approved in current design above:\nUser withdrew the preceding audio-only routing statement as thinking aloud and asks how to make shared instruments, audio clips, track-local devices and common effects intuitive. Do not treat the withdrawn audio statement as a settled restriction. They envision a source/chain picker at beginning of the device strip; shared devices primarily act as instruments.\nPrimary suggestion: make shared instrument chain a MIDI SOURCE choice; its output and track audio clips join BEFORE track-local effects, then pre-fader bounce/fader/output. Audio clips do not implicitly enter the shared instrument or an arbitrary internal suffix. Expose source tile/picker first, followed by clearly local devices. Common reverb/other audio processing can use an EXPLICIT shared audio-effect send/Return instead of pretending instrument and effect inputs are interchangeable. Existing Return/routing contracts provide related foundations. This is a proposal for conversation, not implementation approval or a restriction of previously requested reusable device capabilities. If reusable audio-effect chains are desired, plan them as typed audio-input processors with explicit routing, not guessed injection into an instrument.\nAgreed bounce source isolation, complete track-local/pre-fader capture and fader retention/copy remain. Whether/how shared send/Return effects enter a selected-track bounce remains an OPEN choice; nonlinear shared Return output must not be claimed isolated by muting only its final output. Visual mock shows source/shared instrument, audio source join, local effects, pre-fader tap and separate send/Return. No source implementation authorized.\n
